signal: Nextech was acquired by TPG for $1.4B and launched its AI Cora Scribe, putting new growth pressure on inside sales coverage.

email.body1:
Chad, saw Nextech is scaling under TPG's $1.4B acquisition and just launched the AI Cora Scribe.

Growth at that pace usually means more in-market practices than the inside sales team can cover, and that is where deals quietly go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Nextech off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Chad, quick follow-up for Nextech.

Under new ownership, the pipeline number tends to climb faster than headcount can. Most inside sales leaders don't actually know how many meetings the team needs to hit the new target, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Nextech needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Chad, last bit of proof for Nextech.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire reps fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nextech's reply rate likely compares to similar software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Chad, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding reps isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integration season after an acquisition is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an inside sales motion? I'll tailor it to Nextech either way.
